findings.defect: The resolved-object gate accepts any call whose resolved *types.Func belongs to the own package. A method of an own-package interface (or of a type-parameter constraint) is such an object, so dynamic dispatch to a FOREIGN concrete method is never resolved against the allowlist. Separately, the foreign-state-write rule only inspects assignment LHS selectors, so a write through &pkg.Var is not seen.
findings.counterexample: Compile-valid non-test mutants in the tracked package (go build ./... exit 0) leave TestRepositoryBoundaryAndZeroEffects, TestResolvedObjectEffectBoundary and TestReviewR1CompileValidEffectAndAliasMutants exit 0: (M1) type rvVerifier interface{ Verify(x509.VerifyOptions) ([][]*x509.Certificate, error) }; var v rvVerifier = cert; v.Verify(x509.VerifyOptions{}) => ambient time.Now + system roots (SystemCertPool file I/O on Linux); also via a generic constraint; (M3) type rvLocal interface{ Local() time.Time } => TZ/zoneinfo read; (M2) p := &time.Local; *p = time.UTC => process-global state write. Direct x509 Verify, time.Local assignment, method values, promotion and dot import are refused (controls).
findings.reachability: Not reachable in present production source (no exported-method own interface; only time.UTC read). Defense-in-depth gate only, not cryptographic trusted-process isolation. README states 'certificate Verify/system roots ... are refused', which is not true for this dispatch class.
findings.fix: In sourceEffects: (a) for every used/called *types.Func whose signature receiver is an interface (including type-parameter constraint methods), allow only own-package UNEXPORTED methods (!f.Exported()); refuse own interface or constraint types that declare an exported method or embed a foreign interface (ports.go stays valid); (b) refuse UnaryExpr '&' on any foreign package-level *types.Var and restrict foreign package-level Var uses to an exact read allowlist (today: time.UTC). Add M1/M2/M3 and the generic variant as negatives and an unexported-port call as a pure control. Test-only change plus README wording; no product behaviour change.
